params.body:
## What

This brings gentells.com in line with the designer's maquette C (27 October 2026, eight pages) and the four spoken notes that came with it, one each for the home page, trends, reports and services.

**Home**
- The number band's figures are in the dot face. The rest of the band is unchanged, as the note asks.
- **Latest posts:** the lead post is large, its words on the tall paper beside its picture; the next two are smaller, with their words on the paper strip. All three end on one line, and "More posts" sits at the bottom right.
- **The reports band:** the blur between the cover and the words is gone, and the cover has room around it on the black band. The next reports stand on a light grey, each with its status and title above its cover.
- **Built for professionals:** the three audiences sit around the cluster of torn-paper pieces the designer supplied, each line in capitals. On a phone each audience carries its own piece.
- **Footer:** the page links in sentence case.

**Trends**
- Each generation has its own colour on the filter chips and on the word on each card: Gen Z orange, ZAlpha green, Gen Alpha light blue.
- Each card's image strip shows its sector's picture, so Gaming and Media no longer share a piece of collage. The 12 pictures follow the existing sector-to-topic bridge in `config/taxonomy.php`. The five topics without a sector (Gaming, Fandoms, Music/Film, Social, Sport) keep a piece of collage until the designer delivers their pictures.

**Reports**
- The featured report looks as it does on the home page, with "The Reports" over it.
- The newsletter block at the foot of the page spans the page: the green Gentells wordmark with "this week" on the left; on the right the field under its "Email" label and a button as wide as the field, "Subscribe to Gen Tells This Week".

**Services**
- "Who is it for?" becomes three text blocks with their torn-paper pieces and orange titles, without the coloured cards.

## Decisions to know about

- **Built as the maquette draws it.** This goes beyond the spoken notes, on request. Changes the notes don't mention:
  - the number band in sage, with the figures in a deep sage, labels in capitals and the designer's line on where the signals come from;
  - "Latest Posts" and "The Reports" with their stamp word in dots (`.stamp`);
  - the post card's date as "Seen 22 August 2026";
  - the calls in plain capitals at the maquette's sizes (`.cta-plain`);
  - no status line under a featured report.
- **Dots on the numbers reverse 1 October.** The figures came out of the dot face on 1 October, when the band also carried a second dotted image under the dotted hero. That image is gone, and the maquette draws dots again. Headings other than these two keep their italic word.
- **The designer's colours as drawn, small text included.** They are measured from the maquette: orange `#D9673A`, sage `#9FC7C0`, deep sage `#51716D`, light blue `#ADD2D2`. On white, the orange reads 3.4:1 on the 11-pixel chip labels, and the light blue reads about 1.6:1.
- **What stays as it was:**
  - **The header.** The home page of the maquette draws a green logo and a filled "Create a free account", but its other three pages draw today's header, so every page keeps one header.
  - **The figures stay as floors with a plus** (320,000+). That rounding is a rule about the data, not about the design.
  - **A featured report that is not out yet still shows its date.** The maquette is drawn with a report that is out.
- **Pages drawn in part.** The trends and reports pages appear in part in the maquette: the filters with the cards, and the featured report with the newsletter. The hero, the ticker and the report list in between stay.
- **Wordmark colour.** The wordmark file is drawn in ink, so the green newsletter wordmark gets its colour through a CSS mask (`.wordmark`).
- **Asset sizes.** The supplied elements are converted to WebP: 1 to 65 KB each, 560 KB together.

## Checked

- `tests/Feature/MaquetteCTest.php`, 7 tests:
  - every sector has its picture;
  - a topic gets its own sector's picture and never another's;
  - the card carries its picture and its generation colour, and a lifestage stays grey;
  - the generation colours;
  - the coloured chips on /trends;
  - the dot face on the home page's figures;
  - the newsletter block on /reports.
- Mutation check: six changes undone one at a time, and each turns a test red:
  - the card back to its own picture;
  - Gaming borrowing another sector's picture;
  - the generation word in grey;
  - plain chips;
  - the figures back in the serif;
  - the newsletter back in one line.
- `LiveNumbersTest` now looks for the new sentence on where the signals come from.
- Full suite: 488 of 489. `BuildStampTest` reads the commit from `.git`, which is a file in a git worktree, and fails there without this change too. Pint, ESLint and `bin/lint-tailwind` pass.
- **Seen in a browser:** home, trends, reports and services at desk and phone width, on a local copy seeded with the six reports and six posts currently on gentells.com.
params.title: Maquette C: the home, trends, reports and services pages as the designer drew them
